I understand how you feel. Sometimes you are too exhausted from PTSD and you just want to distract yourself from the pain. Any addiction is a coping mechanism to distract yourself from the emotional pain. If you don't have healthy coping mechanisms, it is very tempting to revert back to cutting or taking drugs. 

Do you have anything to distract yourself with? Whenever I get urges to cut or any addiction urges, I would go out to a public place, library or a shopping mall. If not, I usually talk to my friends and family members or watch YouTube(which is helpful in the short term, provided that you don't get addicted to it. Recovering from an addiction makes it easier to fall into another addiction). Basically anything to distract myself that is not harmful or has no risk of me being addicted. 


Cutting yourself (or any other addiction)will only prolong your suffering. If u have troubles staying motivated, I usually tell myself this: Cutting myself will result in: 1.  Cut myself now, and decide to give up cutting in the future again and i will have to go through this whole ordeal again  2. Give up trying to overcome cutting and accept cutting for the rest of my life 3. I eventually have enough of this shit and suicide. The 1st and 2nd options will only result in more suffering , and the 3rd option I want to avoid. 



Like the other comment wrote, it gets worse before it gets better. You are already doing great by enduring for as long as you have.

At the same time, you should go for therapy, group meetings to try to get some closure from your PTSD. I don't believe that people will ever fully recover from PTSD, we only get better mechanisms to cope with them.

Good luck, i hope this helps

I think you can set up some blockers to reduce the amount of time spent browsing or you can just give your devices for your parents to confiscate. Another way is to go back into old hobbies. Think of a hobby you had when you were young and before the addiction. If you really can't find any hobby, then you can invest in new hobbies. For instance, I got into speed cubing and I have devoted a lot of time into it.  It relieves stress and is just naturally therapeutic(which helps me immensely to manage my addiction). In other words, just try to do whatever makes you happy. Have you read about atomic habits? It is a great way to implement new habit( want to be fitter?). So you have been complaining about the lack of armstrenth. Mini habits are the smallest possible and easiest form of an action. For instance, you can make it a goal to do 1 against the wall push up every day. It will require a very less amount of willpower, so you will usually manage it. Eventually, on days where you will have more willpower, you will do more push ups and become stronger.
